criterion_notes.c1: The paper addresses the Brazilian water and sanitation sector, modeling network expansion (n2, share of population served) in its two-period theoretical model (Section 3) and incorporating municipal water and sewage coverage rates from SNIS in its empirical dataset (Section 4), though coverage enters the regressions only as an explanatory covariate rather than as an access outcome.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, this paper would pass (c2 = yes) because political interference in subnational sanitation regulatory agencies' price-setting during election cycles (alongside tariff regulation and sector controls) is an institutional, regulatory, and governance factor. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification, it fails (c2 = no) in its empirical analysis because the empirical exposure tested is municipal and state electoral cycles (political business/price cycles influencing regulator tariff adjustments), rather than a legal or administrative rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (while Ramsey/price-cap cost-recovery rules for expansion are analyzed only theoretically, and regression controls for contract revisions, the 2020 Novo Marco, and state ownership are neither reported in Table 3 nor tested on any service-access outcome). Even under the plain wording of Criterion 2, however, the full-text decision remains exclude because Criterion 4 (access outcome) fails.
criterion_notes.c3: Section 3 develops a purely theoretical two-period regulatory model, while Section 4 provides quantitative empirical evidence using an unbalanced panel dataset of Brazilian municipalities regulated by subnational sanitation agencies between 2002 and 2021 (N = 1,142 in descriptive statistics; N = 983 in pooled OLS, fixed-effects, and random-effects regressions).
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: the sole empirical dependent variable (outcome) in Section 4 is Variação_real, the annual real percentage adjustment in regulated tariffs approved by sanitation regulatory agencies (nominal adjustment deflated by IPCA), interpreted by the authors as a determinant of firms' financial capacity to invest. System expansion (n2) is modeled purely theoretically in Section 3 and is never empirically tested as an outcome; SNIS municipal water and sewage coverage rates (atend_agua, atend_esgoto) are used only as right-hand-side explanatory variables predicting tariff adjustments, and no household affordability, connection, availability, continuity, quantity, or exclusion outcome is measured.
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis (municipality-year observations under subnational sanitation regulatory agencies in Brazil), exposure (municipal and state election-year dummies), outcome (annual real tariff variation Variação_real), and econometric study design (unbalanced panel pooled OLS, fixed effects, and random effects) are clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with structured abstracts in both Portuguese and English), which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

evidence_quotes.quote: The findings indicate that municipal election cycles are negatively associated with prices set by regulators.

Com o objetivo de testar algumas das predições que podem ser obtidas do modelo, foi construída uma base de dados contendo informações sobre os reajustes anuais aplicados no Brasil no setor de saneamento (para os serviços de água, esgoto ou ambos) entre 2002 e 2021.
Foram também adicionadas variáveis a respeito da abrangência dos serviços de água e esgoto nos municípios, obtidas na base de dados do Sistema Nacional de Informações sobre Saneamento (SNIS).
Em anos eleitorais, o grau de interferência dos políticos (σ) é mais alto sobre a atividade das agências reguladoras. Como resultado, as tarifas praticadas diminuem, em termos reais.
Nessas estimações buscou-se avaliar se em anos eleitorais a variação real das tarifas deﬁnidas pelos reguladores é negativa (o que reduz a capacidade das ﬁrmas de executarem investimentos).

raw_response.exposure: Municipal and state election years (electoral political interference cycles affecting subnational sanitation regulatory agencies), with controls for municipal water and sewage coverage, ordinary contract revisions, post-July 2020 Novo Marco do Saneamento, state vs. private/mixed ownership, municipal GDP, population, and 2020 COVID-19 year
raw_response.outcome: Annual real percentage variation in regulated sanitation tariffs (Variação_real, nominal tariff adjustment deflated by IPCA); network expansion (n2) is derived only in the theoretical model and is not empirically tested
raw_response.population_and_sample: Brazilian municipalities regulated by 88 subnational sanitation regulatory agencies (46 municipal, 26 state, and 16 intermunicipal) from 2002 to 2021 (1,142 municipality-year observations in descriptive statistics; 983 observations in regression estimations)
raw_response.rationale: Exclude (E04 — Wrong outcome; also fails narrow Criterion 2). Although the paper's title and two-period theoretical model (Section 3) examine how political interference in price regulation affects sanitation network expansion (n2), the empirical panel analysis (Section 4, N = 983 municipality-year observations, 2002–2021) tests only annual real regulatory tariff adjustments (Variação_real) as the dependent variable. Municipal water and sewage coverage rates (SNIS) enter the regressions solely as right-hand-side covariates predicting real tariff adjustments, and neither network expansion, household connection/access, nor household affordability is empirically measured as an outcome. In addition, under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, the empirical exposure tested (municipal and state election-year cycles) represents electoral macro-political interference in regulator price-setting rather than a legal or administrative rule-type mechanism directly governing service access; under the plain wording of Criterion 2 it would pass c2, but still be excluded for lacking an empirical access outcome (c4 = no).
raw_response.study_design: Stylized two-period theoretical model and unbalanced panel econometric study (pooled OLS, municipal fixed effects, and random effects)
